notes: V3 DAG L3 #51 - author canonical pheno-fastapi-base Python package.

Package is a standalone flat-layout project at pheno-fastapi-base/ (no src/ parent). Build backend: hatchling. requires-python >=3.11. Runtime deps pinned to the brief: fastapi>=0.110, uvicorn[standard]>=0.27, pydantic>=2.6, structlog>=24.1, plus httpx>=0.27 because AsyncTestClient is part of the public surface. Dev extras: pytest>=8, pytest-asyncio>=0.23, pytest-cov>=4.1, ruff>=0.4, mypy>=1.10. PEP 561 typed (py.typed marker).

Public API: create_app(title, version) -> FastAPI factory that wires /healthz + /readyz probes, StructlogAccessLogMiddleware, register_error_handlers, and a lifespan hook that emits structlog.info('app.started', title=..., version=...) so the JSONRenderer yields exactly {"event": "app.started", "title": ..., "version": ...}. AppError(code, message, details=None, status=None) exception + code_to_status = {NotFound: 404, Validation: 422, Conflict: 409, Storage: 500, Domain: 500}. Handler returns {"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "details": {...}}} with status from exc.status > code_to_status[code] > DEFAULT_STATUS=500. AsyncTestClient is a thin httpx.AsyncClient subclass that pre-wires httpx.ASGITransport(app=app, raise_app_exceptions=True) and exposes a with_app(app) classmethod.

Testing note (gotcha, documented in test docstring): httpx.ASGITransport does NOT propagate ASGI lifespan events. The started-event test drives app.router.lifespan_context directly via 'async with app.router.lifespan_context(app):' instead. This matches the pattern in the FastAPI/Starlette docs for testing lifespans out-of-band.

Structlog config gotcha: configure_structlog sets cache_logger_on_first_use=False intentionally. With caching on, the first structlog.get_logger(...) call after configuration captures a BoundLogger and subsequent structlog.configure() calls are no-ops for that logger. The test suite needs to be able to swap the processor chain between cases (the captured_events fixture), so caching has to be off. The cost is a tiny per-call BoundLogger construction, which structlog measures in single-digit microseconds.

create_app() clobbers the test's structlog capture. The captured_events fixture therefore exposes a .reapply() method that re-installs the capture processor chain. Tests that drive create_app() must call captured_events.reapply() afterwards. The /healthz, /readyz, and AppError tests do not need to capture events so they don't touch the fixture; only the started-event test does.
